'''Marinella Mazzanti''' (born in [[Vinci, Tuscany]], [[Italy]]) is an [[Italians|Italian]] [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic chemist]] specialized in coordination chemistry. She is a professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and the head of the group of Coordination Chemistry at EPFL's School of Basic Sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=GCC|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gcc/|access-date=2021-01-11|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=23 professors appointed at ETH Zurich and EPFL {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen-news/23-professors-appointed-eth-zurich-and-epfl|access-date=2021-01-13|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=2021-01-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115045039/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen-news/23-professors-appointed-eth-zurich-and-epfl|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Marinella Mazzanti|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gcc/mazzanti/|access-date=2021-01-13|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Career ==
After obtaining her "Diploma di Maturità Classica"(Bachelor) from the Liceo Virgilio in Empoli in 1978, Mazzanti studied inorganic chemistry at the [[University of Pisa]] and made her master's degree ("Laurea in Chimica") in 1985. She then joined [[Carlo Floriani]] at the [[University of Lausanne]] as a doctoral student to work low-valent vanadium chemistry. In 1990, she graduated with a PhD (with honors) for her thesis on "Coordination Chemistry of [[Vanadium]] (III) and Vanadium (II)."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chimica di coordinazione del vanadio(III) e del vanadio(II)|url=https://renouvaud.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=41BCU_ALMA7150256020002851&vid=41BCULIB_VU2&search_scope=41BCULIB_ALMA_ALL&tab=default_tab&lang=fr_FR&context=L|access-date=2021-01-15|website=renouvaud.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=MAZZANTI|first1=M.|last2=ROSSET|first2=J.-M.|last3=FLORIANI|first3=C.|last4=CHIESI-VILLA|first4=A.|last5=GUASTINI|first5=C.|date=1989-09-05|title=ChemInform Abstract: N,N′-Ethylenebis(acetylacetoneiminato)titanium Complexes: Synthesis, Crystal Structures, and Properties of Titanium(III) and Titanium(IV) Derivatives.|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/chin.198936286|journal=ChemInform|volume=20|issue=36|doi=10.1002/chin.198936286|issn=0931-7597|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=MAZZANTI|first1=M.|last2=FLORIANI|first2=C.|last3=CHIESI-VILLA|first3=A.|last4=GUASTINI|first4=C.|date=1989-12-05|title=ChemInform Abstract: Phenoxo and Diphenoxo Complexes of Titanium(III) and Vanadium(III): Synthesis and X-Ray Structure.|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/chin.198949239|journal=ChemInform|volume=20|issue=49|doi=10.1002/chin.198949239|issn=0931-7597|url-access=subscription}}</ref> From 1989 to 1991, she was a lecturer in chemistry at the [[University of Lausanne]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mazzanti|first1=M.|last2=Roulet|first2=R.|last3=Schenk|first3=K. == Research ==
Mazzanti's research focuses on research in [[inorganic chemistry]] synthesis and the development of new molecules with novel properties and reactivities. Her research ranges from the development of [[lanthanide]] based [[Luminescence|luminescent]] and magnetic tags for bioanalytical and counterfeiting applications, to the design of [[actinide]] based molecular magnets and to [[small molecule]] activation by complexes of [[Block_(periodic_table)#f-block|f-block]] and [[d-block element|d-block metals]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Di Pietro|first1=Sebastiano|last2=Gautier|first2=Nicholas|last3=Imbert|first3=Daniel|last4=Pécaut|first4=Jacques|last5=Mazzanti|first5=Marinella|date=2016|title=Versatile pyridine-2,6-bis-tetrazolate scaffolds for the formation of highly luminescent lanthanide complexes|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C5DT04811G|journal=Dalton Transactions|language=en|volume=45|issue=8|pages=3429–3442|doi=10.1039/C5DT04811G|pmid=26791092|issn=1477-9226|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Molloy|first1=Jennifer K.|last2=Lincheneau|first2=Christophe|last3=Karimdjy|first3=Maria Moula|last4=Agnese|first4=Fabio|last5=Mattera|first5=Lucia|last6=Gateau|first6=Christelle|last7=Reiss|first7=Peter|last8=Imbert|first8=Daniel|last9=Mazzanti|first9=Marinella|date=2016-03-15|title=Sensitisation of visible and NIR lanthanide emission by InPZnS quantum dots in bi-luminescent hybrids|journal=Chemical Communications|language=en|volume=52|issue=24|pages=4577–4580|doi=10.1039/C6CC01182A|pmid=26941180|issn=1364-548X|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Di Pietro|first1=S.|last2=Imbert|first2=D.|last3=Mazzanti|first3=M.|date=2014|title=An efficient triazole-pyridine-bistetrazolate platform for highly luminescent lanthanide complexes|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C4CC04060K|journal=Chem. Commun.|language=en|volume=50|issue=71|pages=10323–10326|doi=10.1039/C4CC04060K|pmid=25058142|issn=1359-7345|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Among her scientific achievements are the development of highly luminescent [[lanthanide]] complexes that provided insight into structure-properties relationships and enabled applications in bio-analysis and in material science,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Di Pietro|first1=Sebastiano|last2=Gautier|first2=Nicholas|last3=Imbert|first3=Daniel|last4=Pécaut|first4=Jacques|last5=Mazzanti|first5=Marinella|date=2016|title=Versatile pyridine-2,6-bis-tetrazolate scaffolds for the formation of highly luminescent lanthanide complexes|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C5DT04811G|journal=Dalton Transactions|language=en|volume=45|issue=8|pages=3429–3442|doi=10.1039/C5DT04811G|pmid=26791092|issn=1477-9226|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wartenberg|first1=Nicolas|last2=Raccurt|first2=Olivier|last3=Bourgeat-Lami|first3=Elodie|last4=Imbert|first4=Daniel|last5=Mazzanti|first5=Marinella|date=2013-03-04|title=Multicolour Optical Coding from a Series of Luminescent Lanthanide Complexes with a Unique Antenna|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/chem.201203657|journal=Chemistry - A European Journal|language=en|volume=19|issue=10|pages=3477–3482|doi=10.1002/chem.201203657|pmid=23354999|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Andrez|first1=Julie|last2=Bozoklu|first2=Gülay|last3=Nocton|first3=Grégory|last4=Pécaut|first4=Jacques|last5=Scopelliti|first5=Rosario|last6=Dubois|first6=Lionel|last7=Mazzanti|first7=Marinella|date=2015-10-19|title=Lanthanide(II) Complexes Supported by N,O-Donor Tripodal Ligands: Synthesis, Structure, and Ligand-Dependent Redox Behavior|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/chem.201502204|journal=Chemistry - A European Journal|language=en|volume=21|issue=43|pages=15188–15200|doi=10.1002/chem.201502204|pmid=26329984}}</ref> and the establishment of the first synthetic pathway to stable [[pentavalent uranyl complexes]] that led to the development of the first examples of uranium based exchange-coupled single molecules magnets.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Faizova|first1=Radmila|last2=Fadaei‐Tirani|first2=Farzaneh|last3=Bernier‐Latmani|first3=Rizlan|last4=Mazzanti|first4=Marinella|date=2020|title=Ligand-Supported Facile Conversion of Uranyl(VI) into Uranium(IV) in Organic and Aqueous Media|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.201916334|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=59|issue=17|pages=6756–6759|doi=10.1002/anie.201916334|pmid=32017361|s2cid=211023343 |issn=1521-3773}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Teyar|first1=Billel|last2=Boucenina|first2=Seddik|last3=Belkhiri|first3=Lotfi|last4=Le Guennic|first4=Boris|last5=Boucekkine|first5=Abdou|last6=Mazzanti|first6=Marinella|date=2019-08-05|title=Theoretical Investigation of the Electronic Structure and Magnetic Properties of Oxo-Bridged Uranyl(V) Dinuclear and Trinuclear Complexes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.inorgchem.9b01237|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|language=en|volume=58|issue=15|pages=10097–10110|doi=10.1021/acs.inorgchem.9b01237|pmid=31287673|s2cid=195872089 |issn=0020-1669}}</ref>

She is also interested in the design of low-valent complexes of f-block elements, particularly of uranium based transformation processes of small molecules such as [[Nitrogen|dinitrogen]], [[carbon dioxide]] and [[carbon monoxide]] into compounds with higher value.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Camp|first1=Clément|last2=Kefalidis|first2=Christos E.|last3=Pécaut|first3=Jacques|last4=Maron|first4=Laurent|last5=Mazzanti|first5=Marinella|date=2013|title=Controlled Thermolysis of Uranium (Alkoxy)siloxy Complexes: A Route to Polymetallic Complexes of Low-Valent Uranium|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.201307291|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=52|issue=48|pages=12646–12650|doi=10.1002/anie.201307291|pmid=24123544|issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

On example is her identification of polymetallic architectures that facilitate the cleavage of dinitrogen and its subsequent utilization in synthesis coupled with [[carbon dioxide]], protons or [[carbon monoxide]]. Such polymetallic architectures based on f-block elements involve multimetallic and [[Metal-ligand cooperativity|ligand-metal cooperativity]], and allow for the extension of this concept to other transition metals.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jori|first1=Nadir|last2=Falcone|first2=Marta|last3=Scopelliti|first3=Rosario|last4=Mazzanti|first4=Marinella|date=2020-05-11|title=Carbon Dioxide Reduction by Multimetallic Uranium(IV) Complexes Supported by Redox-Active Schiff Base Ligands|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.organomet.9b00792|journal=Organometallics|language=en|volume=39|issue=9|pages=1590–1601|doi=10.1021/acs.organomet.9b00792|s2cid=214141334 |issn=0276-7333}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Willauer|first1=Aurélien R.|last2=Toniolo|first2=Davide|last3=Fadaei-Tirani|first3=Farzaneh|last4=Yang|first4=Yan|last5=Laurent|first5=Maron|last6=Mazzanti|first6=Marinella|date=2019|title=Carbon dioxide reduction by dinuclear Yb( ii ) and Sm( ii ) complexes supported by siloxide ligands|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C9DT00554D|journal=Dalton Transactions|language=en|volume=48|issue=18|pages=6100–6110|doi=10.1039/C9DT00554D|pmid=30869730|s2cid=76664963 |issn=1477-9226}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
Mazzanti is the recipient of the 2023 LeCoq de Boisbaudran award in f-elements chemistry
Mazzanti is the recipient of the 2021 ACS Albert Cotton award in synthetic inorganic chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=ACS 2021 national award winners|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/awards/ACS-2021-national-award-winners/98/i31|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-15|website=ACS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=F. Albert Cotton Award in Synthetic Inorganic Chemistry|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/f-albert-cotton-award-in-synthetic-inorganic-chemistry.html|access-date=2021-01-15|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref> She was 2019 Randolph T. Major Lecturer at the [[University of Connecticut]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Randolph T. Major Lecture Series|url=http://www.events.foundation.uconn.edu/ehome/406223/858155/|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.events.foundation.uconn.edu}}</ref> 2016 Rubin Colloquium Technion Lecturer at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Israel Institute of Technology]] in [[Haifa]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Small Molecule Activation by Low-valent f Elements – שוליך|url=https://chemistry.technion.ac.il/events/small-molecule-activation-by-low-valent-f-elements/?lang=he|access-date=2021-01-15|website=chemistry.technion.ac.il}}</ref> and 2009 [[Glenn T. Seaborg]] Memorial Lecturer at [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In 1994 she was awarded with the [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions|Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mazzanti, MER Marinella - École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne EPFL - Institute of Chemical Sciences and Engineering|url=https://www.x-mol.com/university/faculty/2749|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.x-mol.com}}</ref>

Mazzanti has been a member of editorial board of [[Helvetica Chimica Acta]] (since 2017),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Helvetica Chimica Acta|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/15222675/homepage/editorialboard.html|access-date=2021-01-15|website=Wiley Online Library|language=en}}</ref> editorial board of [[Dalton Transactions|Dalton Transaction]] (since 2017),<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Welcoming our newest Editorial Board member: Marinella Mazzanti – Dalton Transactions Blog|url=https://blogs.rsc.org/dt/2017/02/01/welcoming-our-newest-editorial-board-member-marinella-mazzanti/|access-date=2021-01-15|language=en-US}}</ref> and advisory board of [[Inorganic chemistry|Inorganic Chemistry]] (2011-2014).<ref name=":3" />

She was a member of the management committee of the European Network COST D-38,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Curriculum Vitae : Dr. Marinella Mazzanti|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/gcc/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/CVMazzanti.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=EPFL}}</ref> of the international organizing committee of the Rare Earth Research Conference<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Advisory Board – 29th Rare Earth Research Conference (RERC29)|url=https://web.sas.upenn.edu/rerc29/about/international-advisory-board/|access-date=2021-01-15|website=web.sas.upenn.edu}}</ref> and of the Actinides international conference.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Event :: 10th International Conference on f-Elements (ICFE-10) :: ChemistryViews|url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/event/11083190/10th_International_Conference_on_f-Elements_ICFE-10.html|access-date=2021-01-15|website=www.chemistryviews.org}}</ref> She was a coordinator of [[Agence nationale de la recherche]] (ANR) and [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] (SNFS) funded projects.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SNSF {{!}} P3 Research Database {{!}} Project 162430|url=http://p3.snf.ch/|access-date=2021-01-15|website=p3.snf.ch|language=en}}</ref>
